By looking at the implementation of `FastDateFormat.getInstance(String pattern)`, it seems this method returns an instance of `FastDateFormat` without any explicit serialization logic.

The `SerializationUtils.serialize(Serializable obj)` method converts a `Serializable` object into a byte array for serialization. This method is likely used to serialize the `FastDateFormat` instance in the test.

The `mRules` field in `FastDateFormat` is declared as `private Rule[] mRules;`. This array of rules is likely not being handled properly during serialization and deserialization, leading to the reported issue.

To fix this problem, we can make the `mRules` field transient to exclude it from the serialization process. We would also need to add custom deserialization logic to initialize `mRules` after deserialization. 

The following method should be fixed:
```java
org.apache.commons.lang.time.FastDateFormat.mRules
```

Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
